description: A web application that remote-controls running `chief serve` instances. Built with Laravel 12 + Inertia.js + Vue 3 + Tailwind CSS 4, hosted on Laravel Cloud. The web app performs zero AI work — it is a relay, cache, and account system that communicates with chief servers running on users' machines or VPSes via WebSocket (Laravel Reverb). The primary use case is "check on your phone" — monitoring runs, reviewing progress, and managing projects from anywhere.

userStories.title: Device OAuth Flow — Endpoints
userStories.description: As a chief CLI instance, I want to authenticate via device OAuth flow so that I can securely connect without copy-pasting tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /oauth/device/code — accepts { device_name }, returns { device_code, user_code, verification_uri, expires_in, interval }. Generates human-readable user code (e.g., ABCD-1234). Stores in oauth_device_codes with 15-minute expiry.

POST /oauth/device/token — accepts { device_code }, returns access token + refresh token on approval, or { error: "authorization_pending" } / { error: "slow_down" } / { error: "expired_token" }. Access token: 1-hour expiry. Refresh token: 90-day expiry.
POST /oauth/token — accepts { grant_type: "refresh_token", refresh_token }. Rotates the refresh token (old one invalidated, new one issued). Returns new access + refresh tokens.
POST /oauth/revoke — accepts { token }. Revokes the refresh token, marks device_authorizations.revoked_at.

POST /oauth/device/exchange — accepts a one-time setup token (generated during VPS provisioning in US-038), returns access + refresh tokens. Token is single-use and expires after 10 minutes. Used for automated VPS auth so the user doesn't need to manually run chief login on cloud-deployed servers.
Rate limit: device code requests limited to 10 per IP per 15 minutes
Rate limit: token polling enforces minimum 5-second interval per device code (returns slow_down error if faster)
Rate limit: token refresh limited to 30 per device per hour
All endpoints return proper OAuth 2.0 error responses

userStories.title: Reverb Setup & Server WebSocket Authentication
userStories.description: As a chief server, I want to establish a WebSocket connection to chiefloop.com so that I can relay data to the web app.
acceptanceCriteria: Laravel Reverb configured and running as a separate process
Chief servers connect to wss://chiefloop.com/ws/server — no token in the URL

Authentication happens via the first message (hello): { "type": "hello", "protocol_version": 1, "chief_version": "0.5.0", "device_name": "...", "os": "linux", "arch": "amd64", "access_token": "eyJ..." }
On valid hello: respond with { "type": "welcome", ... }, resolve token to user and device, register connection, mark device online, store chief_version/os/arch in device_authorizations
On invalid/expired/revoked token in hello: respond with { "type": "auth_failed", "code": "AUTH_FAILED", "message": "..." } and close the connection
Reject (ignore and log) any messages received before a valid hello
If the access token expires during an active connection, server sends auth_refresh_required message
On disconnection, device status is updated (triggers "Reconnecting" → "Offline" flow)
Connection events (connect/disconnect) are broadcast to the user's browser channel

userStories.title: Browser Echo Integration
userStories.description: As a browser client, I want to receive real-time updates via WebSocket so that the UI stays current without polling.
acceptanceCriteria: Laravel Echo configured in the Vue frontend connecting to Reverb
Browsers subscribe to a private channel scoped to their user ID (private-user.{userId})
Browsers can also subscribe to device-specific channels (private-device.{deviceId})
Channel authorization via Laravel's standard broadcast auth
Echo connection status reflected in the UI (connected/reconnecting indicator)
Reconnection is automatic with exponential backoff
On reconnect, missed messages are replayed from Redis buffer

userStories.title: Redis Message Buffering & Replay

acceptanceCriteria: All bufferable WebSocket messages are stored in Redis: claude_output, run_progress, run_complete, run_paused, clone_progress, session_timeout_warning, error, quota_exhausted
Key pattern: ws:buffer:{device_id}:{session_id}
Buffer cap: 5MB per session (configurable via env var)
Oldest messages evicted when cap is exceeded
On browser reconnect, buffered messages are replayed in order
Buffer is kept for 5-minute grace period after chief server disconnects, then flushed
State snapshots and project lists are not buffered (re-requested on reconnect)
Buffer cleanup runs via scheduled task (no stale data accumulation)

userStories.title: WebSocket Message Relay

Messages pass through with minimal processing; the web app updates its cache as messages flow through
If the target device is offline, commands return an error: "Server offline"
Message format is JSON with a type field and a payload field
Invalid/malformed messages from chief are logged and discarded (no crash)

Handle RATE_LIMITED error responses from chief (code: RATE_LIMITED, includes retry_after hint). Chief enforces its own rate limits (30/s burst, 10/s sustained; 2/min for expensive ops). On receiving a rate limit error, the web app surfaces it to the browser as a toast: "Server busy — retrying in [N] seconds" and automatically retries after the retry_after period

userStories.title: UI Quality Audit & Interaction Polish
userStories.description: As a user, I want every interaction to feel premium and intentional so that using the app is a delight.
acceptanceCriteria: Animation audit: Every animation serves a purpose. No gratuitous motion. Entrances inform spatial hierarchy (where did this come from?). Exits confirm dismissal. Progress indicates work happening. Transitions maintain context (where am I going?).

Timing consistency: All similar animations use the same duration — micro (100ms: toggles, state changes), standard (200ms: modals, dropdowns, page transitions), slow (300ms: complex reveals, accordions). No animation exceeds 400ms.

60fps audit: Scroll all pages, open all modals, trigger all animations with DevTools Performance panel open. Zero jank. All animated properties use transform and opacity only (GPU-composited). No layout-triggering animations.

Touch audit (mobile): Navigate every screen on a real mobile device (or emulator). Every interactive element is easily tappable. No accidental taps from elements being too close. Scrolling is never hijacked. No dead zones.
Keyboard audit (desktop): Navigate every screen using only the keyboard. Tab order is logical. Focus is always visible. No focus traps (except modals). All actions are keyboard-accessible.

Color contrast audit: Run automated contrast check (axe-core or similar). All text passes WCAG AA. All interactive elements are distinguishable from non-interactive ones. Status colors are distinguishable for colorblind users (use shape + color, not color alone).
State completeness audit: Every component handles all states: default, hover, focus, active/pressed, disabled, loading, error, success, empty. No missing states.
Responsive audit: Resize browser from 320px to 2560px width. No layout breaks, no horizontal scroll, no overlapping elements, no truncated text without ellipsis, no orphaned elements at any width.

Error recovery audit: Trigger every possible error (network down, server offline, invalid input, expired session, rate limited). Every error is recoverable without a page refresh. User always knows what happened and what to do next.

Optimistic UI audit: All user-initiated actions (start run, pause, save settings, send message) reflect immediately in the UI. Server confirmation updates happen without visual disruption. Rollbacks on failure use a subtle shake + error toast pattern.

Copy-paste audit: All copyable elements (SSH commands, IPs, device codes, URLs) work with single click. "Copied!" confirmation is visible. Pasting into inputs works correctly (device code, repo URL, API key).

Consistency audit: Same action looks and behaves the same everywhere. "Save" always looks the same. "Delete" always has the same confirmation pattern. Status dots always mean the same thing. Spacing and typography are consistent across all pages.
Performance audit: Lighthouse score > 90 for Performance on both mobile and desktop. Time to Interactive < 3s. No unnecessary re-renders (verify with Vue DevTools).

userStories.title: Accessibility
userStories.description: As a user with accessibility needs, I want the app to work with assistive technologies so that everyone can use it.
acceptanceCriteria: All images and icons have appropriate alt text or aria-label
All form fields have associated <label> elements
